findings.title: Mitel Product Security Advisory MISA-2026-0012
findings.summary_md: Mitel's MISA-2026-0012 disclosed five unauthenticated AWV flaws in MiCollab, including CVE-2026-133324, and rates the authentication bypass Medium at CVSS 5.3. Supported MiCollab 10.3 (10.3.0.18) and earlier are affected; the remedy is to upgrade to 10.3.0.18 and apply the KB000129195 patch, or move to a later release. Mitel advises restricting external access to AWV until the fix is implemented.

findings.title: CVE Record: CVE-2026-133324
findings.summary_md: The CVE record describes CVE-2026-133324 as improper authentication handling in MiCollab's AWV component, permitting an unauthenticated authentication bypass and unauthorized actions within the application. It assigns CWE-636 and CVSS 3.1 5.3 with no confidentiality or availability impact and low integrity impact. The record lists MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) as affected.

findings.title: When patch day comes too late: MiCollab flaws exploited before disclosure
findings.summary_md: Accenture APEX Labs reported pre-disclosure exploitation of the five MiCollab AWV flaws in MISA-2026-0012. At one victim, web-shell activity preceded Mitel's November 16 advisory; the actor reached root within 30 minutes and used MiCollab's LDAP connector credentials against a domain controller at T+32 minutes. A second victim had communicated with the same actor infrastructure since November 9, but its initial access vector was not established.

findings.title: CISA Adds 10 Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
findings.summary_md: CISA added CVE-2026-133324 and four other MiCollab AWV vulnerabilities to KEV based on evidence of active exploitation. The catalog gives CVE-2026-133324 a November 28, 2026 federal remediation deadline and marks ransomware campaign use as unknown.

findings.title: Mitel MiCollab Zero-Days Exploited in Suspected AI-Assisted Attacks
findings.summary_md: SecurityWeek reported Accenture's finding that attackers exploited several MiCollab AWV flaws before Mitel's November 16 advisory. At the confirmed victim, commands ran 12 minutes after the first request, root was reached within 30 minutes, and internal backup and database servers were accessed roughly 20 hours later. The actor was not attributed, and evidence of commercial AI API use was assessed as possible assistance rather than proof of fully autonomous exploitation.
